panels.description: Wide, full page width. The coast seen from the fort wall. Low clouds over the sea, their underbellies dark grey. Husk fires in the fishing village send smoke lying flat along the sand. Far out on the grey water, a few Dutch ships at anchor, small and grey.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The day before Colachel smelled of coconut smoke and rain that had not yet fallen.

panels.description: Nagoji on the rampart, three-quarter back view, facing the sea. The waves below roll in low and sluggish. The air is visibly heavy: haze, no wind in the palms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Even the waves seemed to be waiting for something.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We waited with them.

panels.description: A boy at the top of a palm-trunk lookout tower, one hand shading his eyes, the other arm flung toward the sea, calling down to a runner at the foot of the tower.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Reports came in all day.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From the palm tower: Dutch sails furled and unfurled like nervous fingers.

panels.description: Ibrahim Marakkar at the fort gate, wringing seawater out of his coat sleeve, grinning. Short and broad, scar from the LEFT ear to the jaw, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets. Behind him a dripping Marakkar cousin: taller and thinner than Ibrahim, bare-chested in a checked lungi, no coat, no scar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From Ibrahim and his Marakkar cousins: supply craft cut loose in the night, anchors sabotaged.

panels.description: Tight insert. A palm-leaf list of chiefs' names incised in fine lines (no legible script). Ramayyan's stylus held still above one name. The point has stopped.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From the inland chiefs, men mustering. Some eager, some sullen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kottarakkara sent nothing.

panels.description: Ramayyan Dalawa seated at a low writing desk in the anteroom of the war hall: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundles and stylus. Nagoji standing at his shoulder in the rust-red turban. Ramayyan's eyes do not leave the leaf.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And Kottarakkara?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Some absences speak louder than presence.

panels.description: Padmini Amma in the doorway, overhearing, leaning on her long walking stick. Fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for walking. A sound that is not quite a laugh.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The Thekkumkur Raja counts Dutch masts and waits to see which way the wind blows.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Savitri in Kottarakkara writes letters to Velinadu asking whether this is the moment.

panels.description: Nagoji's face, turning from her to Ramayyan. Ramayyan's stylus moves on.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She did not say what moment. She did not need to.

panels.description: Insert. An unrolled palm-leaf ola strip in Padmini's hand, its cord hanging loose with a small lac seal on the thread; incised lines only, no legible script.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From Revathi Bayi in Velinadu: she would remain within her halls, her men ready to move if the Dutch threatened their share of the coast.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words were correct, empty of warmth.

panels.description: Padmini reading it a second time, the leaf lowered, her eyes on the middle distance.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: She is watching too.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Watching to see whether her king is worth her kinswoman's silence.

panels.description: Morning. A pepper ridge above terraced fields: pepper vines climbing the trunks of support trees, green berry spikes hanging. Padmini barefoot on a bund, sari hitched, stick in hand, pointing up at the ridge vines. A village headman beside her; men and women bent over the vines below.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Padmini Amma moved through all of this like a pivot.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You will not take the vines on that ridge. If the Dutch burn the lower fields, we will still have pepper to sell them at higher prices when they crawl back.

panels.description: The headman grinning, caught out. Padmini is already walking on.

copy.speaker: HEADMAN
copy.text: Always thinking of profit, Amma.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Profit is survival written in accounts.

panels.description: Noon. The fort rampart. The tip of her stick on stone. Nagoji a pace behind her. Below, men hauling shot along the wall.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (small)
copy.text: The walls will hold.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (smaller)
copy.text: If the men do.

panels.description: Inset, small, set into the lower corner of 4.1. Afternoon. Her hands counting bolts of cloth and measures of grain into the arms of soldiers' wives.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Fear is heavy enough without empty stomachs.

panels.description: Sunset at her estate. Boys carrying oil jars toward the temple; women lighting lamps in doorways. Under the great jackfruit tree in her yard, Padmini and Nagoji facing each other.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You will ride from here in the morning. Your horses will leave hoofprints in my yard. Do not waste them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will try not to trample anything you wish to keep.

panels.description: Bottom strip. Padmini close, her face lit orange by the last light, looking past him toward the sea.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The sea and the Dutch will trample more than you ever could.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Just make sure that when they do, they taste sand with it.

panels.description: Wide. Daylight under the low cloud. Horsemen walking their horses slowly along the tide line, hooves in the shallow wash, a long loose file: Madurai riders on heavier horses, with lances and bright high-wrapped turbans; Maravar riders on smaller ponies, bare-headed, white mundus hitched, short jackets. Nagoji at the head on Kayal, his bay mare with an ochre red-brown coat, no white markings.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Earlier that day.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: While she moved through her layers of responsibility, I moved through mine.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was too late to teach new tricks.

panels.description: Two riders on the wet sand. Nagoji in the left foreground on Kayal (ochre-bay mare), rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash. Ponnan half a length back on the right on a smaller Maravar pony: broad-shouldered, bare-headed, short curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, short dark jacket, white mundu hitched.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: Tomorrow we do not have the luxury of turning when we please. They will fire when it suits them, not us.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then make the sand your ally before their powder speaks.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You and your men read this beach better than any Deccan rider.

panels.description: Ponnan alone on his Maravar pony: bare-headed, short curly hair, heavy jaw, red shoulder cloth, short dark jacket. A soft snort, his eyes on the sea, not on the man beside him.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: If we live through this, Sawant, I will decide whether to be flattered.

panels.description: Nagoji turned in the saddle on Kayal, addressing the whole file. Faces listening: bright Madurai turbans, bare Maravar heads.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You do not have to kill every Dutchman to win. You have to break their line, their nerve.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If you survive one volley and reach them still moving, half their courage will die before any man does.

panels.description: Raza Khan on his heavier Madurai horse, adjusting his green high-wrapped turban: lean, hawk nose, pointed moustache, a puckered scar on his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek (our right as he faces us), three-quarter view with that cheek toward camera. Nagoji at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: We have fought men with guns before. But we have not fought men who think their God has given them all the guns that matter.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then we teach their God some humility.

panels.description: Wide. The fort courtyard. Nair footsoldiers sitting in groups: bare-chested, white mundus tied short, hair in front topknots, no coats or uniforms. They clean matchlock muskets, check powder flasks, tie talismans around wrists and upper arms; round shields and swords stacked nearby. One mutters over his hands. Another laughs with his head thrown back.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some joked too loudly, voices a shade too high.

panels.description: Nagoji crouching to the level of a group of young Nair soldiers: bare-chested, front topknots, matchlocks across their knees.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have seen their ships now. Do they look like gods?

panels.description: One young Nair soldier (bare-chested, front topknot) laughing, nervously.

copy.speaker: YOUNG NAIR
copy.text: They look like houses turned on their sides.

copy.speaker: YOUNG NAIR
copy.text: With too many sticks.

panels.description: Nagoji turning to a second, older-faced young Nair who is not laughing, bare-chested, a matchlock upright between his knees.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the men on them?

copy.speaker: SECOND NAIR
copy.text: They look like men. Too pale. Too stiff.

panels.description: Nagoji standing, close on his face, the courtyard behind him out of focus.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Good. Remember that when they fire.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Their powder burns the same. Their blood spills the same.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Their screams sound the same when steel touches them.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall. On a low table, a hand-drawn ink map on cloth: coastline, rivers and hills as lines only, no lettering, no place names, no compass rose; pebbles and shells as tokens. Marthanda Varma over the map in complete stillness: V13 face, cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested, a spear leaning within reach. Standing beside him, Mathoo Tharakan: older, grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, white cloth, a gold cross prominent on his chest. Ramayyan seated cross-legged at the end of the table with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Nagoji standing across the table.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Mathoo Tharakan, a Syrian Christian merchant from the north, with eyes as sharp as Ramayyan's stylus.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They are here because their books are bleeding.

panels.description: Varma's finger tracing the inked coastline on the cloth map (lines only, no lettering); a glance at the standing Mathoo Tharakan, grey moustache, gold cross on his chest.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They are angry that we refuse their contracts and sell instead through men like Tharakan here.

copy.speaker: THARAKAN
copy.text: Their anger is cheaper than their pepper, Your Highness. Let them keep it.

panels.description: Inset, tight, set into the lower right of 8.2, on the map beside Varma's tracing finger. Ramayyan's thin fingers setting a small copper Dutch coin, its face too small to read, on the coast mark for Colachel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had learned by then not to mistake him for a clerk.

panels.description: Ramayyan, seated with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus, looking up from the coin. A rare hint of satisfaction.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen him lead men against Kollam, breaking their lines with the same precision he used to balance accounts.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They are overconfident. And they are alone.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Dutch are fighting their own fires in the east. What sits on that beach is all they have.

panels.description: Mathoo Tharakan (grey moustache, gold cross) and Varma, two profiles over the cloth map.

copy.speaker: THARAKAN
copy.text: Van Imhoff meant to strangle the chumkam, the crown's share of every bag of pepper that leaves this coast. No treasury, no army.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: A sailor's strategy. But he forgets that pepper has legs.

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width. A cutaway: a line of bullock carts climbing a ghat pass inland, heaped with pepper sacks, Syrian Christian merchants walking beside the wheels. Empty sea far behind them.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (voice-over)
copy.text: The Dutch can blockade our harbours until their ships rot, but they cannot stop a bullock cart.

panels.description: Flashback, desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. Wide. Colachel town from a distance, smoke rising from burning roofs, the ships' guns as small flashes offshore, people streaming inland along a palm road.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Last November.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three days, and then they sailed away. It was only a message, written in salt and ash: we can reach you.

panels.description: Flashback, desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. February dawn. Longboats beaching; VOC soldiers in blue coats wading ashore under cannon smoke from the ships; Travancore Nair soldiers (bare-chested, white mundus tied short, front topknots, matchlocks, no coats or uniforms) falling back into the dunes and palm forest.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In February, they came back to stay.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: What followed was not war as the Deccan knew it. It was a strangling.

panels.description: Flashback, desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. Tengapattanam, from the shore at a great distance. Burned houses and a scorched temple roof still smoking. A longboat pulling out toward a ship, small shapes of women and children in it, oars rising. Nothing close.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (memory)
copy.text: They sold prisoners as slaves. Twelve and a half rixdollars for anyone over fourteen.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (memory)
copy.text: Twenty for a Nair, because Nairs are worth more to the Batavia markets.

panels.description: Flashback, desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. The half-built Dutch fort. A mud bastion slumping under the weight of a cannon, earth sliding off it. Sacks rotting in the open. Sick soldiers lying in thin shade. Inset in the lower corner of this panel: Karl August, pale with a sickly yellow cast, cropped greying hair, rough cotton shirt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Karl August, a German deserter. Our eyes inside the Dutch mind.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST (memory)
copy.text: Their engineer builds today, demolishes tomorrow. When they put nine cannons on the walls, the weight made them collapse.

panels.description: Flashback, desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. Full width. Ships standing out to sea under full sail; on the beach behind them, a thin line of blue-coated VOC soldiers and an unfinished wall, watching them go.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST (memory)
copy.text: Hackert, their commander, left. He took most of the ships, the rice, the gunpowder. He left a lieutenant named Rijtel with two hundred and fifty Europeans.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST (memory)
copy.text: They have provisions for days, not weeks.

panels.description: Back in the war hall, present colour. Small brass oil lamps have been lit. Ramayyan seated with his palm leaves, his face set; Varma straightening from the cloth map (ink lines only, no lettering); Nagoji across the table.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Desinganadu promised to fight us, then stopped his campaign because of a festival. A festival.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Coalitions built on Dutch coin fall apart when the coin stops flowing.

panels.description: Nagoji leaning in, a hand flat on the map. Varma cutting across him, not raising his voice.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If we charge them...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No charge. Not yet.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We do not spend men to prove we are brave. We spend them to win.

panels.description: Overhead on the cloth map (ink lines only, no lettering, no compass rose). Varma's hand sweeping a line of pebble tokens inland across the road behind the Colachel coast mark, closing it. The copper coin sits on the coast.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We pin them. Block the inland road. Force them back onto the sand.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: A siege? On an open beach?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: A prison without walls.

panels.description: Inset, set into the upper corner of 12.3, over the sea side of the map. The sea at night: Mukkuvar kattumaram log rafts, three to five rough logs lashed together, low in the water, fishermen kneeling and paddling, no sails, no lights, slipping between dark Dutch hulls.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (voice-over)
copy.text: And the sea?

copy.speaker: VARMA (voice-over)
copy.text: At night, the sea will belong to the fishermen, not the Dutch ships.

panels.description: Varma turned full on Nagoji. Direct, level.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Your horsemen will not charge a line, Nagoji. You will be the bars of the cage.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Capture their scouts. Cut off their foraging parties.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Once they step onto that beach, they never step off it unless in chains.

panels.description: Bottom strip. Nagoji and Varma face to face over the map, the coin between them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was a colder plan than a dawn charge.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We will starve them. And bleed them.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We will break them. Slowly. Until they realise that their monopoly is worth less than their lives.

panels.description: Wide. The temple near the fort in a thin drizzle: a Kerala temple with a laterite outer wall and low sloping tiled roofs. Long rows of small oil lamps along the outer wall. Men and women passing with cupped palms held to the flames, some pressing the warmth to their eyelids and chests.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A puja not for harvest or marriage, but to steady hands that would hold weapons at dawn.

panels.description: Padmini at the inner gate handing small packets of kumkum and ash to Nair soldiers (bare-chested, white mundus tied short, front topknots). One ties it at his wrist. A few Madurai riders in bright high-wrapped turbans hang back at the edge of the light, respectful and wary.

Ibrahim Marakkar (short and broad, scar from the LEFT ear to the jaw, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets) setting a small brass lamp from the shore mosque on the lowest temple step, its light joining the others. Nagoji beside him.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The sea does not care whose name you call when it takes you.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Best to have several listening.

panels.description: Raza Khan (green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache) and his Madurai men standing apart, palms raised in their own prayer, facing west, lips moving.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We had all come from somewhere else. Tomorrow we would bleed into the same sand.

panels.description: Ibrahim (short coat, broad back) and Nagoji from behind, looking out at the dark line of the sea. Far out, the tiny lights of a few Dutch ships.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You think they pray on those ships?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They pray to their god and their profit. I do not know which they trust more.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: We will find out tomorrow.

panels.description: Wide. The estate at night. A man sitting on a step tracing his sleeping child's face with his fingertips. A woman checking a rice jar. On a shelf behind her, folded white cloth set within reach.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Women checked that clothes for mourning lay where they could be found if needed.

panels.description: Under the jackfruit tree, lit by a small brass oil lamp with an open wick set on the ground, no glass chimney. On the left, Dhanaji on a low stool, sharpening his talwar with a whetstone in long strokes: stockier and heavier than Nagoji, a short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic, no sash. On the right, Nagoji sitting across from him in the rust-red turban and red sash, clean-shaven chin, talwar across his knees.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Dhanaji. He had survived Goa's dungeons alongside me.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You ever think you would be here, sahib? About to ride at Dutch guns for a king who is not yours?

panels.description: Nagoji, the corner of a smile, lamplight from below.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The gods have poor handwriting.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If they wrote this in my horoscope, the astrologer must have fallen asleep.

panels.description: Dhanaji (short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic), the whetstone still on the blade, serious now.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: The men trust you. When you say "ride", they will.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That is what frightens me.

panels.description: Wide. The two men small under the jackfruit tree, the brass lamp between them. Dhanaji on the left (short black beard, white pagdi turban) looking up, surprised. Nagoji on the right (rust-red turban) looking at the lamp, not at him. Behind them in the dark, riders asleep on mats and the horse lines, heads low.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You are not afraid of Dutch guns?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Guns I understand. Men who follow because they believe you see further than they do, that is a weight I am still learning how to carry.

panels.description: Dhanaji (short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic), the blade laid across his knees, his gaze softened.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You carried it on the Godavari.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You carried it when you chose to jump from that ship and leave a boy behind rather than let both of you drown for nothing. Do not pretend this is new.

panels.description: Nagoji's face, still, in the lamplight. Behind him, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: black storm water; a rope tearing through bandaged palms, its free end whipping loose, tied to no one; beyond it, Keshavrao (young, narrow shoulders, black hair hacked short, prisoner rags, no scar, no coat) sinking with his ankles still chained in a pair. No rope near his neck or body.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The mention of Keshavrao landed like a stone in my chest.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It feels different here. There, we rode for hills we knew.

panels.description: The two men in the circle of lamplight. Dhanaji on the left (short black beard, white pagdi turban) taking up the whetstone again as he answers. Nagoji on the right (rust-red turban), his thumb moving on the talwar hilt across his knees.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Here, I ride for a king I have known a short while, on land whose gods I do not fully understand.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: The bullets will not stop to ask whose gods you prayed to. You ride for the man you chose when you did not run north.

panels.description: Padmini stepping into the lamplight, her stick silent on the damp earth, looking down at Nagoji (seated, rust-red turban).

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You men speak of guns and gods. But there are older powers to reckon with before the sun rises.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Come, Nagoji. There is one place you must visit.

panels.description: Full width. Padmini leading Nagoji past raised wooden granaries on stone footings with tiled roofs, toward a thicket of trees looming like a dark island at the edge of the estate. The canopy swallows the few stars.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: This is the Sarpa Kavu.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The Abode of Snakes.

panels.description: Large, half the page. The clearing at the heart of the grove. Roots coiling over the ground like solid serpents. Termite mounds rising like small stupas. Hundreds of granite serpent idols, hoods spread, coiled, singly and intertwined, beneath one massive tree. At the foot of the largest idol, Revathi Bayi lighting a small oil lamp: deep indigo sari with gold, a shawl against the damp, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, a sandalwood line at the hairline. No tali.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The air smelled of wet stone, camphor, and rotting leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi Bayi.

panels.description: Revathi turning from the lamp, her face lit from below.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: It is a secret place. Only the immediate family of Padmini Amma's tharavadu may walk here freely.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: To bring a stranger is to ask the Naga Rajas to witness him.

panels.description: Padmini bowing her head before the stone serpents. Nagoji a pace behind her, barefoot on the leaf litter, turban and talwar kept.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He rides for us. He needs their permission to bleed on their earth.

panels.description: Revathi, one hand open toward the idols.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Before there were kings in Padmanabhapuram, before the Dutch sailed their wooden islands, this grove was here.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We let the Nagas rule this darkness so that they might let us rule the light.

panels.description: Close on a stone cobra hood, lamp flame reflected in its carved eye.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: We ask for their blessing. Not for glory, but for venom.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: The stillness that strikes.

panels.description: Revathi looking past the idols into the dark. Leaves hanging motionless.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: There is a moment, before every great event, when the land holds its breath.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This is that moment. The Naga lords are listening.

panels.description: Revathi's eyes finding Nagoji's.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We do not shout our war cries here. We endure. We bend until men think we will break, then we stand up again.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That is the lesson of the snake.

panels.description: Padmini kneeling, fingertips raised from the earth to her forehead. Nagoji beside her, barefoot.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Pray, Nagoji. Ask that your strike be true.

panels.description: Nagoji, eyes closed, lamplight on half his face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not pray for victory.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I prayed for the focus of the cobra, the patience of the stone.

panels.description: Nagoji's eyes open. Beside him, only the stones and an empty patch of leaf litter. Revathi alone by the lamp, her composure slipping.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (unsteady)
copy.text: Good. Now go.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (unsteady)
copy.text: Sleep if you can.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji has stepped forward and pulled Revathi into a tight embrace. She has melted against him, her face in his shoulder, shaking. The lamp and the serpents small around them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a heartbeat, the war vanished.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I only wanted to remain here, anchoring myself to this woman, for a lifetime.

panels.description: Close. Nagoji's mouth near Revathi's hair, the words costing him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If I survive, we will have a conversation about queens and guests.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But not tonight.

panels.description: Revathi has pulled back just far enough to look at him, tears on her cheeks, voice rough.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You do not get to die cheaply now. Not with unfinished words between us.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then I will try to live expensively.

panels.description: Inset, small, set into the upper right corner of 20.3. Far off through the black tree trunks, a single point of lamplight at the house.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI (off, distant)
copy.text: Nagoji?

panels.description: Revathi, cheeks just wiped, a sad, knowing smile, stepping close to him again. Her whisper has an edge.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And Nagoji... if you die tomorrow, die facing the right direction.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Do not give the Dutch the satisfaction of seeing your back.

panels.description: Full width, bottom strip. In the foreground, Revathi's fingers brushing the coils of a stone serpent; beyond, her face at Nagoji's ear, eyes lowered.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (whisper)
copy.text: And if you live, do not make me a widow for a king I did not choose.

panels.description: Revathi turned back to the idols, a shape in the lamp glow. At the edge of the grove, Padmini emerging from the shadows to guide Nagoji out, his boots in his hand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Only the memory of her fragrance hung in the humid air, to torture me.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The dawn will not wait. Rest now.

panels.description: Nagoji lying on a mat in a dark room, turban set aside, eyes open.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Sleep came in fragments.

panels.description: One panel split into three narrow slivers, left to right. First: close on bandaged hands and the iron bar across chained ankles, against the damp curved wall of the Goan cellar. Second: black storm water, a rope tearing through bandaged palms, its free end whipping loose, tied to no one; beyond, Keshavrao (young, narrow shoulders, black hair hacked short, prisoner rags, no scar, no coat) sinking with his ankles still chained in a pair, no rope near his neck or body. Third: wet sand, horses pounding, blue-coated VOC soldiers firing through smoke, and in the smoke, Revathi's sorrowful smile.

Dream, in the page 10 treatment: desaturated palette, soft borderless edges. Nagoji alone on an empty beach, the horizon tilted. On one side the fort's silhouette, too tall and too close; on the other the sea, flat and glassy. Palms and blown sand streaming sideways in the wind. No other people, no footprints.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The last fragment. The sound of drums, carrying on the wind.

panels.description: Full width. The estate yard in the grey before sunrise, under the great jackfruit tree. Riders saddling horses; fresh hoofprints churned into the damp earth. In the foreground Nagoji, rust-red turban re-tied, boots on, buckling on his talwar beside Kayal, his bay mare with an ochre red-brown coat. Men turning their heads toward the sound: far off beyond the palms, the dark line of the fort wall with tiny drummer silhouettes on it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When the real drums began, they sounded exactly like the ones in my dream.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The eve was over.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: The storm was here.

frames.review_note: Minor: a few small puddles on the laterite rampart floor suggest earlier rain, while the caption says the rain had not yet fallen. They read as old monsoon wet, so this is acceptable. Low dark-bellied clouds, flat husk-fire smoke along the beach and three small grey ships at anchor all match the script. No text in the art. The wide cloud band at the top leaves room for the caption.

Minor: the surf shows some whitecaps rather than truly sluggish waves, but the haze and still palms carry the heavy-air beat. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a gold ear stud. He is in three-quarter back view on the same laterite rampart, with the same domed sentry turret as 1.1. The grey sky on the upper right has room for both captions.

Minor: the boy faces out to sea rather than turning down toward the runner, though the runner at the foot of the tower is clearly looking up at him. The beat reads: one hand shades his eyes and the other arm is flung toward the sea from the top of a lashed palm-trunk tower. Anatomy is sound and there is no text. A large open sky on the right takes both captions.

Minor: the ground at the gate is puddled, which hints at rain, though dripping seawater and earlier monsoon wet can explain it. The cousin has a beard, which the script does not forbid. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, short teal coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, the scar on his LEFT side from ear to jaw, short and broad, and grinning. He wrings teal coat cloth at his cuff while water drips, and his hands are sound. The cousin is taller and thinner, bare-chested in a checked lungi, with no coat and no scar. The fort gate is the same laterite as 1.1 and 1.2. The sky on the upper right has room for the caption.

Usable tight insert: an aged hand in plain white cloth holds an iron stylus still over a corded palm leaf on a low wooden desk on a woven mat, with a brass oil lamp. No face is shown, so there is nothing to check against Ramayyan's sheet beyond the hand and white cloth, and both fit. The lower 40% of the frame is plain dark wood, a clean place for both captions. Small faults: (1) the incised rows are tally-like pseudo-glyphs rather than plain fine lines, and a few strokes look letter-like ('a', 'e', 'r') under zoom, but nothing is legible and at reading size they read as scratched entries in a list; (2) the stylus tip touches the leaf at the end of a row instead of hovering just above a name, though it still reads as a point that has stopped; (3) the warm lamplight mood differs from the prompt's grey overcast daylight, which matters little for an insert; (4) under close zoom the middle fingertip on each side of the stylus looks slightly doubled, which cannot be seen at print size.

Minor only: the background banners carry a gold elephant on red rather than the Travancore silver conch (no lettering), and the courtyard stones look damp under overcast haze, with no falling rain visible. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Ramayyan matches his sheet and keeps his eyes on the leaf. The red laterite wall above Ramayyan and to the right of Nagoji's head leaves ample space for both balloons in reading order.

Minor only: she is stepping over the threshold rather than standing and leaning in the doorway, but she is still in the doorway, using the stick, with a dry half-smile that fits 'not quite a laugh'. She matches her sheet and the bible: thick black hair coiled at the nape with no grey, a gold ball earring and bead necklace, the cream sari with a gold border in the Kerala drape with no blouse, and the long stick. Hands and feet are sound and there is no text. The large plain laterite wall on the right (about x 0.60 to 0.95, y 0.05 to 0.55) takes both balloons easily.

Minor only: there is a faint stipple of skin texture on Nagoji's jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven, and Ramayyan's writing desk is doubled into two stacked low tables. Nagoji matches the bible: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging from it, long curly black hair, cream tunic and red sash. His eyes turn toward Ramayyan, who keeps writing with a stylus on a palm-leaf bundle. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, no marks. The brass lamp has an open wick and there is no text. The plain laterite wall at upper right (about x 0.60 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.30) gives clean space for the caption.

None significant. The insert is tight on the leaf: a long, narrow palm-leaf strip with fine incised lines only and no script, held in Padmini's left hand. A braided red cord with a small round lac seal hangs from a hole at the far end, and the seal shows no letters. Her right hand grips the stick, and both hands have the right number of fingers and sound anatomy. The cream and gold sari and gold bangles match her sheet. The room and the overcast doorway continue panel 2.2. The plain dark laterite wall at upper right (about x 0.62 to 0.92, y 0.02 to 0.28) holds both captions without covering the hand or the leaf.

Forced pick past the two-correction stopping rule (Claude, 2026-10-08). v04 is a hand retouch of v02 (see HAND-RETOUCH-2026-10-08.json): Padmini alone in the anteroom, on model, eyes on the middle distance, leaf lowered, clear wall for both balloons. The faint pseudo-text on the leaf is smoothed away. Remaining fault for the author: the leaf is a short, broad tag with a pale cord, not the long narrow ola strip with the red braided cord of 2.4.

Minor: Padmini's black hair falls in loose curls to her shoulders, so the nape coil is not clearly visible (colour, face, gold stud earrings, necklace, cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse, walking stick and bare feet all match her sheet). The workers pick pepper beside and slightly below the bund rather than well below it. The lettering space is the top-left sky and the misty hills: the caption fits in the top-left corner and Padmini's long balloon fits across the upper sky above her and the headman's heads. No painted text, balloons or anachronisms. Pepper grows on living support trees and the hands are sound.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet and bible line: cream sari with a gold border, old drape with no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold earrings and necklace, stick, barefoot. She is already walking on past the grinning headman, whose hands are pressed together, which reads well as being caught out. The pepper vines are on living support trees, with terraced paddy behind. There is no text and the hands are sound. Minor points: two small background women (upper left and lower right) appear to wear short-sleeved blouses. They are tiny, matching the earlier precedent of tolerated background blouses. This headman (moustache only, white head-band) differs from the bearded headman in 3.1 v01, so 3.1 is being regenerated to match this one. Lettering: Padmini's balloon goes in the open sky to the right of her head (upper centre-right). The headman's short balloon goes at the top between his head and hers, overlapping the foliage at top left if needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the commander sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only faint shading, a tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, brass-hilted sword as on his sheet, and boots. Padmini matches her sheet. The setting is a laterite rampart under midday overcast light, with Dutch ships at anchor offshore. Men below along the wall haul cannon on ropes beside stacked shot. Flags are plain red with no marks. There is no text and the anatomy is sound. Deviations: Nagoji walks nearly level beside her rather than a full pace behind. The tip of her stick runs out of the bottom of the frame instead of being shown on the stone. Her right hand hangs close to Nagoji's scabbard tip, a slight tangent that still reads as depth. Lettering: the large open sky at upper right easily takes both small Padmini balloons. The 3.4 inset should go in the lower-right corner, over the wall and shot, not the lower left, where Nagoji's boots are.

Acceptable for a small hands-only inset. Padmini's cream sari with its gold border, her gold bangle and her stick hand identify her. Her other hand rests on folded bolts of cloth while soldiers' wives take cloth and a measure of rice from the baskets in a laterite storeroom, with the fort visible through the doorway. That is the afternoon beat. Every hand is sound: four hands on the measure and the cloth, each traced to a wrist and arm. The flag in the doorway carries only a dark emblem, with no lettering. Minor: the cropped wife at upper right shows a short rust-red sleeve under her green drape, likely a stitched blouse. It is small and cropped at inset size, so it is noted but tolerated. Padmini's face is out of frame, so her balloon tail points to the top edge above her neckline (upper left). Lettering: the plain laterite wall at top centre, between the cloth stacks and the doorway.

Acceptable. This fixes the round-1 sleeve fault: both of Nagoji's tunic sleeves come down to the wrists, and no forearm skin, brand or scar shows. Nagoji matches his commander sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, tiny flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, cream tunic, broad red sash, talwar held at the scabbard, boots. Padmini matches her sheet: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold studs, necklace and bangle, cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with her chest covered, stick, barefoot. She gestures to him with an open palm while he faces her. The setting matches the script and 3.6: sunset estate yard, the great jackfruit tree over a worn stone platform, horse lines along the compound wall, jar carriers with brass jars, and women on the pillared verandah of the tiled Nair house lighting brass lamps with open flames. There is no text, and the hands are sound. Minor points: the jar carriers read as grown men rather than boys, and the yard lamps are tall brass stands, which is in period. Lettering: Padmini's long balloon goes in the orange sky and palm silhouettes at upper left, above her head and left of the trunk. Nagoji's balloon goes over the canopy and roof at upper centre-right, above his turban, with a tail down to his mouth.

Acceptable. Padmini in close-up matches her sheet: thick black hair coiled at the nape (the faint silvery lines read as sheen, not grey), gold stud earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, gold bangle, hand on her stick. Her face is lit warm orange by the last light. She looks right, past the frame, toward the sea and the setting sun. The setting is the same as 3.5 (Nair house with brass lamps, jackfruit tree over the stone platform, horse lines at the compound wall). There is no text and the hand is sound. Minor: one horse in the line at far right is white or grey, while the horse line in 3.5 is all dark, and the bible keeps greys out of the Madurai troop. It is small and at the frame edge. Lettering: the open orange sky at upper right, between the jackfruit foliage and the sun, takes both Padmini balloons, with tails running left to her mouth.

Minor. Nagoji's ear ornament sits as a tiny gold bead just below the lobe. At 6x zoom it reads as a small drop rather than a flush stud. It is about 7 px tall in the frame and reads as a gold dot at panel size, but it is a known stud deviation to list for the author. Everything else fixes the r1 failure. Every Madurai rider wears a white high-wrapped turban and white jama, carries a bamboo lance and rides a dark horse, with no green turban anywhere. The Maravar riders are bare-headed with curly hair, short dark jackets and hitched white mundus, on lighter, smaller ponies. Nagoji leads on the right in his rust turban, cream tunic, red sash and boots, with sleeves to the wrist, a clean chin and a curled moustache. Kayal is an ochre bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs, and no white. The scene is overcast, with hooves in the shallow wash and palms inland. The whole upper-left sky is open for three captions.

Minor. The small, soft background riders on the far left wear dark turbans and red cross-sashes, and one wears a rust-red turban. That does not match 4.1's white-turbaned Madurai file and bare-headed Maravar riders, and the bible bans red or rust Madurai turbans. Their heads are only about 3% of frame height, so they cannot be identified at print size. Ponnan wears dark shoes in the stirrup where his sheet is barefoot, and his jacket is plain brown where 4.3 has black with gold trim. The principals are correct: Nagoji (clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, rust turban, red sash) is in the left foreground on Kayal (ochre bay, no white), and Ponnan is half a length back on the right on a smaller dark-bay pony (bare-headed, curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu). There is a large open sky band for all three balloons.

Minor. Ponnan's pony has a small white star on the forehead and is a lighter chestnut-bay than the dark-bay pony in 4.2. With no other horse in frame, it does not read as especially small. His jacket is black with gold trim, matching his sheet's trim but differing from 4.2's plain brown. Ponnan matches his sheet: bare-headed, short curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu, bare feet in the stirrups. He is alone on the beach, gaze off toward the sea. The open overcast sky on the right takes his balloon easily.

Minor. Two of the Maravar riders on the right wear tiny gold earrings. The r1 correction asked that only Nagoji wear one, but these men cannot be confused with him. Both r1 failures are fixed. No green turban appears: every Madurai lancer on the left wears a white turban and white jama. The Maravar riders now wear short dark short-sleeved jackets with white mundus and bare legs, matching 4.1 and 4.3. Nagoji is turned in the saddle with his arm out and his palm open, addressing the file, and both groups look at him. He matches his sheet: clean chin, curled moustache, a tiny gold stud on the lobe, rust turban, red sash, sleeves to the wrist and boots. Kayal is an ochre bay with no white markings. The upper-right sky is open and low-detail for both balloons.

Minor. Nagoji's left sleeve is pushed up to mid-forearm. Only the outer forearm shows, with no brand or scar drawn, but the prompt asks for sleeves to the wrist, as he has in 4.1 and 4.4. Background Madurai lancers appear although the prompt called the troop off-frame. They wear white turbans and fit the beach file of the neighbouring panels. The r1 failures are fixed. Kayal has a plain ochre bay face with no star. No background rider wears green. Nagoji sits at the left edge, cropped, so Raza is the subject. Raza matches his sheet: deep green high-wrapped turban, green drape, lean hawk face, pointed moustache and grey-streaked goatee. His scar is on his anatomical LEFT cheek, turned toward camera, and his hand is raised to adjust the turban. Nagoji has a clean chin, a curled moustache and a small stud on the lobe. The open sky across the top centre and upper right takes both balloons clear of the faces and of Raza's raised hand.

Minor only: topknots sit on the crown rather than at the front, and one torch burns in daylight. Otherwise it shows the beat: bare-chested Nairs in white mundus cleaning muskets, powder flask, talisman tied on an upper arm, one muttering over his hands, one laughing with head thrown back, shields and swords stacked. Plain unlettered flags. The cloudy sky across the top leaves room for the caption.

Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, sleeves to the wrists, red sash, boots, talwar. He crouches among young bare-chested Nairs who have muskets across their knees, and his hands are sound. Minor: three tiny out-of-focus figures in the gateway (around x 0.82, y 0.33) wear brimmed European-looking hats. They are barely legible at print size. The cloudy sky top-left and top-centre is clear for the balloon.

Clean. The young bare-chested Nair with a topknot laughs nervously, hand behind his head and musket held upright. The courtyard and gatehouse match 5.1 and 5.2, and the hands are sound. Minor: the topknot sits on the crown, and the muskets read as flintlocks across the page. The open sky above and left of him has room for both balloons.

Minor only: light stipple texture on Nagoji's jaw reads as shading, not a beard. The second Nair wears his topknot on the crown, not at the front. Lettering space is the grey sky band across the top left and centre, which is narrower than ideal but fits two short balloons above the heads. Otherwise clean: Nagoji matches the sheet (rust turban, curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, sleeves down, boots, talwar) and turns toward an unsmiling, bare-chested older Nair who holds a matchlock upright between his knees. The setting is the laterite courtyard with a tiled gatehouse under grey cloud. No text, no doubles, and the hands are sound.

Minor only: faint stipple on the chin and jaw (smooth enough to read as clean-shaven). The background is simplified rather than strongly blurred, but it still reads as soft and secondary. Close on Nagoji with a set jaw: rust turban, thick curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, cream tunic and red sash. The courtyard with Nair soldiers, matchlocks and shields matches 5.4. The large grey-sky area at the upper right easily holds the three Nagoji balloons without touching his face.

Minor only: brass lamps are already lit in daylight, though 8.1 says lamps 'have been lit' later. Nagoji's scabbard reads a little straight for a talwar. All four principals match their sheets. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, a clean chin, the curled moustache and the gold stud. Varma has black hair with a knot on his left side and is bare-chested in cream and gold. Tharakan has grey hair, a grey moustache and the gold cross. Ramayyan sits cross-legged with his bundle and stylus. The map is lines only and there is no text. The open sky band above the table has room for the caption and Varma's balloon. Use this frame as the anchor for Varma's look on the rest of the page.

Acceptable, with minor issues only. The beat works: Varma leans over the cloth map, his index finger traces the inked coastline at centre-left, and his eyes turn up and sideways to glance at the standing Tharakan. Varma has jet-black hair with no grey, the white-and-red namam, a pearl ear drop, a bare chest, gold bead necklaces and a cream mundu with a gold border, with no turban, crest or crown. His hair is wavier and fuller than the sheet's sleek look, and the knot sits at the top-back of his head rather than clearly above the left ear. Both of those match how he is drawn in the picked 6.1 and 6.5, so the page stays consistent. His moustache is a little thicker than the sheet's thin waxed one. Tharakan matches his sheet: grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross, white cloth with gold borders and the palm-leaf ledger. He holds a small dark object in his left hand, which is harmless. The setting is the same open seaward war hall as 6.1 and 6.5: tiled roof, timber pillars, plain white banners, overcast daylight and a ship at sea. The map is lines only, there is no text anywhere, and the hands are sound. A small brass lamp is lit in daylight, as in 6.1. The lower right holds a lamp, a cup and a rolled cloth. The 6.3 inset will simply cover them, since nothing important is there. For lettering, Varma's balloon can go over the roof at upper left or in the sky between the pillars, and Tharakan's in the open sky at upper right. That gives a natural left-to-right reading order.

Clean. A tight inset. A hand in a white cloth sleeve, read as Ramayyan's, pinches a small plain copper coin with no readable face onto the inked coast mark, beside a pointing index finger from the right (Varma's tracing finger). The map is lines and stipple only, with pebble and shell tokens and no lettering. Minor: Ramayyan's hand looks more weathered than 'thin', but the anatomy is sound. Plain cloth in the upper right holds the caption.

Minor only: the cloth map on the table is turned, with the sea on its right side where 6.1 has it on the left. A brass lamp is lit in daylight. Otherwise clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet and 6.1: receding hairline, curly black side hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. He sits cross-legged, looking up with a faint satisfied smile. The hands are sound, there is no text, and the hall and sky are the same as 6.1. The large open sky in the centre and right has room for the caption and both Ramayyan balloons.

Acceptable. Two facing profiles over the cloth map. Tharakan on the left matches his sheet: grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross and white cloth with gold borders. Varma on the right has BLACK hair knotted at the back of his head (as in 6.1), the sheet's moustache, a bare chest, gold bead necklaces and a cream mundu with a gold border, with no turban or crest. Minor: Varma has a small white forehead mark (his sheet has one) and no visible ear drop. The setting is the same open seaward war hall with brass lamps and grey light. A large clear sky between and above the two heads holds both balloons. The hands are sound and there is no text.

Clean. A full-width strip of a line of bullock carts on solid wooden wheels, heaped with roped pepper sacks, climbs a red-earth ghat road. Merchants in white mundus and shoulder cloths walk beside the wheels. An empty grey sea lies far behind on the left, with no ships, horses or spoked wagons. A wide, quiet overcast sky across the top third holds the voice-over box. Most merchants are seen from behind, so no face is truly readable; the listed heads are the nearest ones. RAMAYYAN (voice-over) is lettered as a tailless box under the script's notes, so the tail point (left edge, toward the coast and the war hall) is only nominal.

Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failure: no blue coats, tricornes or other Europeans appear anywhere on land. The wide, distant view of Colachel shows burning tiled and thatched roofs with smoke columns, Dutch ships offshore with gun flashes, and townsfolk with bullock carts, baskets and children streaming up a palm road. A few bare-chested Nair men in white mundus, with topknots and long guns, walk among them. There is no text, signature, blood or bodies, and no visible anatomy faults; every figure is seen from behind, so no faces can be read. The large grey sky in the upper right is clear for both captions. Minor points: the palette is muted blue-grey rather than strongly desaturated, the muzzle flashes are bigger than 'small', and there are shot-splash columns around the ships. None of these breaks the beat.

Clean. Longboats are beaching at dawn under cannon smoke from the ships; VOC soldiers in blue coats and tricornes wade ashore; the Nair soldiers are bare-chested, in white mundus tied short, with front topknots and long guns, falling back into the dunes and palms. No text, blood or bad anatomy. The upper-left sky is clear for both captions. The palette is a little warmer than 7.1 and 7.3 but still muted.

Acceptable, and it addresses the r1 rejection. Tengapattanam is seen from a rocky shore at a great distance: burned palm-thatch frames and a Kerala-style tiled temple roof with blackened, scorched patches, smoke drifting over the water. There is no stone fort, bastion, castle or lighthouse. A single longboat pulls toward an anchored ship, carrying veiled women and small children seen from behind, rowed by two standing men in drab tunics (not red coats). There is no text on the ship or anywhere else, and no blood, ropes or chains. The open upper-right sky gives ample room for both Ramayyan memory balloons. Minor points: the oars are dipped rather than rising, the women's head veils read slightly generic, and the foreground rocks are heavy. Ramayyan is off-panel narrating from the present, so the tail points are nominal: the lower-left edge, toward the viewer's shore position, matching the off-panel convention used in 7.5.

Acceptable. Karl August matches his sheet: cropped grey hair, grey moustache and stubble, a gaunt sallow face, a stained rough cotton shirt. He sits in a soft-edged vignette inset in the lower-left corner. The half-built fort has scaffolding and a mud bastion slumping under a cannon, with earth sliding off. There are rotting sacks and puddles, and sick blue-coated soldiers lie under a thin awning. The flag is plain horizontal red, white and blue bands with no monogram, and there is no text. The upper-right sky is clear for the caption and Karl's memory box. Minor: the distant departing ships slightly anticipate 7.5, and Karl's yellow cast is mild (sallow rather than jaundiced).

Clean. This is a full-width strip: ships under full sail standing out to sea with plain tricolour flags and no lettering, and a thin line of blue-coated VOC soldiers on the beach watching them go beside the unfinished mud wall, cannon and awning. It matches 7.4's fort, so the page stays consistent. A wide open sky across the top holds both Karl memory boxes. The palette is somewhat bluer and brighter than a strict desaturated flashback, but in line with 7.4. Karl is off-panel and his lines are tailless memory boxes, so the tail points are nominal (lower-left edge, toward where his inset sat in 7.4).

Acceptable with minor faults. The cast is correct: Nagoji on the left in the commander look (rust-red turban, red sash, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, small gold stud), Ramayyan seated in the centre with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus (receding hair, clean-shaven, plain white), and Varma on the right (bare-headed, bare-chested, gold necklaces, cream mundu with gold border) with a hand on the map. The night war hall with small brass open-wick lamps is right, the map has ink lines only with no text, and there is clear night sky and roof for both balloons, Ramayyan's first and Varma's second. Minor faults: (1) Nagoji has light stippled stubble on his chin and jaw. At print size it reads as shading, but the bible asks for a clean chin. (2) Varma has a whitish-grey streak at his temple, and his hair is in a crown knot, not a side knot above the LEFT ear (the same crown knot as page 6). (3) Nagoji's sleeves are pushed up, and the brand shows as a pale blurred patch on his crossed LEFT forearm. The ch13 row allows this. (4) Nagoji stands at the end of the table, not exactly across it.

Acceptable. The beat reads clearly: Nagoji leans in with his left hand flat on the map, and Varma cuts across him with a calm raised palm. Nagoji's chin is essentially clean, with a thick curled moustache, a gold stud and the commander dress. Varma's face matches his sheet, with black hair, gold beads and a cream and gold mundu.
